name: Turntech
old_description: Founded in April of 2002 by Curvin & Lucille Horning, Turntech started in a 2-car garage with one hydraulic copy lathe and a dream. Not to mention a mini fridge stocked with Mountain Dew and peanut butter cups!
about:
Turntech was founded in April 2002 by Curvin and Lucille Horning in Ephrata, Pennsylvania. The company began in a two-car garage equipped with a single hydraulic copy lathe, marking the start of a family-owned woodworking operation in Lancaster County.

Today, Turntech produces a wide range of custom wood turnings, including columns, porch posts, mouldings, kitchen island legs, balls, and dowels. The shop operates a custom CNC lathe capable of turning pieces up to 17.5 inches in diameter and 144 inches in length, and works with species such as walnut, cherry, mahogany, maple, oak, cedar, pine, and poplar. The team can replicate historic profiles through reeding, rope twisting, barley twisting, and fluting, and accepts customer-provided photos, sketches, or CAD drawings for made-to-order projects.

Customers include contractors restoring historic properties, homeowners updating entryways or staircases, furniture makers, and even martial-arts practitioners sourcing wooden balls. The company has supplied half a dozen porch columns for a historic restoration and recreated a lyre for a Duncan Phyfe chair, demonstrating its ability to handle both architectural and decorative commissions.

Turntech emphasizes domestic production, shipping custom orders in as little as five business days, and the ability to match existing designs exactly. The founders highlight a blend of old-world craftsmanship with modern technology, a commitment to employing local craftsmen, and community involvement in Lancaster County.
